title: pi settings — pi's core schema plus this machine's extension keys
description: IntelliSense for a pi `settings.json`. Core keys come from pi's own published schema; the extension branch documents the three top-level keys pi knows nothing about: `modelFallback`, `startupFetch`, `piBolt`. Neither branch constrains unknown keys, so a key owned by an extension pi has never heard of stays valid.
$comment: The core half is upstream-owned: pi generates it from its TypeScript source and ships a copy at `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/schemas/settings.schema.json`. After a pi upgrade, diff that local copy against the `$ref`'d URL to see what changed — and nothing here. This wrapper redeclares no core key on purpose: core keys are pi's to document, and only the three below can drift from the local code that reads them.

allOf.$comment: Extension-owned keys, each described from the reader named in it. `additionalProperties` is deliberately unset here: pi never validates settings, and its own write path preserves keys it does not know, so closing this object would paint a working extension's config red.

modelFallback.description: The model router in `agent/extensions/model-fallback/`: it registers the virtual model `fallback/auto` and hands a failed request to the next entry in `chain`. pi ignores this key. The extension reads it at load time — before pi's settings API exists — from this file, or from a project's `.pi/settings.json`, whose whole object replaces this one rather than merging key by key.

enabled.description: Set false to stop a process registering `fallback/auto` at all, leaving failover to pi's own retry. It does not switch off a chain a parent already launched this child on (`PI_FALLBACK_CHAIN`): such a process cannot resolve its own model without the router.

chain.description: Models in priority order — the first is the primary, each later entry takes over while the one before it keeps failing. Malformed entries are dropped at startup with a warning naming each one and why; a `chain` that is present but not an array warns too, and contributes nothing.

anyOf.description: `provider/modelId`, or a bare id pi resolves unambiguously. The provider may be a virtual one an extension registered, so it is not checked against any list. A `|` level suffix is the env and agent-file grammar and is dropped here: the object form owns pins in this file.
The same reference, plus the thinking level to pin while the router holds it. Unknown properties are ignored by the router, so a typo in one is otherwise invisible.

model.description: `provider/modelId`, matched by pi's own rules: canonical `provider/id`, then provider plus id, then bare id. A `:level` suffix, a leading or trailing `/`, commas and internal whitespace are rejected — and a rejected reference drops the whole entry, because it names no model to route to.

thinking.description: Thinking level pinned for requests to this model. Case-sensitive and untrimmed: a value outside the list is dropped while the model is kept, so the session's own level governs.

maxCycles.description: Laps of the whole chain allowed in one failure burst — a cap on laps, not per model — so it is the router's analogue of `retry.maxRetries`. Keep `retry.maxRetries` at least `chain length × maxCycles` or the physical budget gives up before the router has used the chain. Anything that is not a positive integer is replaced by 10.

maxProbes.description: Consecutive failed hand-backs to the primary before the fallback that is actually answering becomes the new home. Anything that is not a positive integer is replaced by 2.

concurrency.description: In-flight caps per model, held as leases in one shared directory (`PI_MODEL_FALLBACK_LEASE_DIR`), so two sessions against the same gateway obey one cap instead of two. `"*"` sets the default for every model the map does not name; a model with neither entry nor default is uncapped. A key that is not a usable model reference, or a value that is not a positive integer, is ignored at startup — the model is silently left uncapped, so this squiggle is the only notice you get.

.*.description: The cap for the model this key names (`provider/modelId`, any casing); `"*"` is the default for all the others.

groups.description: Named sets of models sharing one global cap — several replicas of one deployment, where per-model caps would let each run its own. Read independently of `concurrency`, so a config with only `groups` is valid. An invalid entry is dropped silently at startup, with no warning to say a cap went missing: a `name` blank after trimming, a `max` that is not a positive integer, or a `models` list that is empty or holds anything that is not a plain `provider/modelId`.

name.description: The group's label. Control characters are stripped and it is trimmed, so a blank string is not a name; two groups with the same name (compared case-insensitively) keep the first.

items.description: A member as `provider/modelId`, any casing, deduped. A `|` level pin drops the whole group: it is the chain grammar, which can never match a lease key, so the shared cap would silently run looser than configured. A `"*"` member is only skipped, and the group survives without it — but a `models` list left empty that way drops the group, since `minItems` cannot see what parsing removed.

max.description: How many members of this group may be in flight at once, across every process sharing the lease directory.

contextWindow.description: Context window advertised for `fallback/auto` before the first response arrives, for the context-usage readout only. It cannot be derived from the chain: the model catalogue is not readable when the virtual model is registered, which is load time. Once a model has answered, that model's own limits govern — compaction included. Absent means no claim is made.

maxTokens.description: Maximum output tokens advertised for `fallback/auto` before the first response, for the same readout and the same reason as `contextWindow`.

anyOf.description: Shorthand: a bare array is read as the chain itself (`modelFallback: ["a/b", "c/d"]`), with every other option at its default.

`provider/modelId`, or a bare id pi resolves unambiguously. The provider may be a virtual one an extension registered, so it is not checked against any list. A `|` level suffix is the env and agent-file grammar and is dropped here: the object form owns pins in this file.
The same reference, plus the thinking level to pin while the router holds it. Unknown properties are ignored by the router, so a typo in one is otherwise invisible.

model.description: `provider/modelId`, matched by pi's own rules: canonical `provider/id`, then provider plus id, then bare id. A `:level` suffix, a leading or trailing `/`, commas and internal whitespace are rejected — and a rejected reference drops the whole entry, because it names no model to route to.

thinking.description: Thinking level pinned for requests to this model. Case-sensitive and untrimmed: a value outside the list is dropped while the model is kept, so the session's own level governs.

startupFetch.description: The picture drawn in the startup header by `agent/extensions/startup-fetch.ts`. Read on every header build, so an edit applies on `/reload` without a restart; a file this key cannot parse is read as an empty object.

mode.description: How the picture is chosen from `<agentDir>/images/`: `fixed` always shows `image`, `cycle` takes the next file by name on each start and wraps, `random` picks one avoiding an immediate repeat, `off` prints the ASCII distro logo instead. Any other value is treated as `fixed`.

image.description: A file name inside `images/`, or an absolute or `~`-prefixed path to a file anywhere. Only consulted in `fixed` mode.

style.description: How the image is drawn in terminal cells, coarse to fine. `block` and `half` go through catimg; `quad`, `sextant`, `octant`, `braille` and `ascii` go through chafa and fall back to `half` when it is missing; `pixels` sends real pixels over the Kitty graphics protocol and falls back to `half` on a terminal that has no Kitty (or iTerm2) support. Any other value is treated as `half`.

height.description: Rows of terminal cells the drawing gets. A value outside 4–40, or a non-integer, is replaced by 13 rather than clamped to the nearest bound.

piBolt.description: The Pi-Bolt-only half of the package list (https://github.com/opensec-git/Pi-Bolt, pi compiled ahead of time). Plain pi ignores this key entirely, which is the point: both binaries share one `settings.json`, and a swap that lives only here cannot make plain pi load the build meant for the other one.

items.description: One package source, in pi's own grammar (`npm:name[@version]`, `git:github.com/owner/repo`), where a leading `-` removes that source and a bare entry adds one.

packages.description: Package sources this overlay contributes — on top of `packages`, or instead of it when `packagesOverlay` is set. Typically `-npm:@ff-labs/pi-fff` plus the JIT-free build's name, since the upstream package needs bun's FFI. Only entries that are strings are read; the rest are skipped.

packagesOverlay.description: When true, `piBolt.packages` replaces the effective `packages` list — additions minus removals — instead of merging into it, which is what keeps the replaced name out of the declared set. It takes effect only together with an array `packages`, and the persona extension applies the same rule when it works out which sources a profile declares.
